recipes.name: Irish Soda Bread with Caraway Seeds

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9-inch round cast iron skillet or a 9-inch round baking or cake pan.
Combine flour (reserving 1 tablespoon), sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, raisins and caraway seeds in a large bowl.

Blend eggs, buttermilk and sour cream together in a small bowl; stir into flour mixture until flour is just moistened. Knead dough in bowl about 10 to 12 strokes. Dough will be sticky. Place the dough in the prepared skillet or pan and pat down. Cut a 4x¾ inch deep slit in the top of the bread. Dust with reserved flour.
Bake in the preheated oven for 65 to 75 minutes. Let cool and turn bread onto a wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Irish Soda Bread with Caraway Seeds
raw_recipe.description: This soda bread recipe made with flour, baking soda, buttermilk, sour cream, and caraway seeds is sweetened with raisins. Best served warm with butter.

review.reviewBody: My Great grandmother (also from Ireland) used a very similar recipe; this is the only other time that I have seen it calling for the 'X' on the top. However, we use melted butter/margarine (1 cube melted) instead of the sour cream and we scale the raisins down to approximately 3/4 to 1 cup; we dip the knife into the flour and then make our 'X'. We don't put seeds in ours. This was the first recipe that my cousins and I were taught to make when we were young girls, or 'wee ones' as our Grandmother called us. For some strange reason, the best bonnets (Great grandma said that they weren't loaves but "bonnets of bread") seemed to come from my mother's oven...an old Wedgewood. Now they come from my kitchen...I have an 'old Wedgewood' now.

Made it yesterday-first attempt. Trying to use up sour cream and buttermilk. Took advice of some reviewers and reduced raisins (had only golden in pantry) to (2) cups and added 1/2 cup chopped apricots. Increased buttermilk slightly because I had only 1/2 cup sour cream. Good thing I read reviews re stickiness of dough otherwise I probably would have added too much flour. I did use a cast iron skillet and also followed a reviewer's comments -- cut the cross in on top after 15 minutes in oven. The dough was so sticky. Followed another reviewer's comments -- just plop it into a greased pan, spray back of spatula with Pam and smooth top. Came out great. 

I don't digest butter easily and this recipe doesn't have it as an ingredient and so I hope it freezes well. I could consume the whole loaf -- had to get it out of sight.
Loved it! I decreased raisins to 1 cup and cooked in conversation oven for 45min at 325.

This recipe is "Tried and True" I used a scant 2 cups of "plumped in hot water" raisins. I used 1 teaspoon of caraway. Next time I will use either 1 1/2 teaspoons or 2 teaspoons caraway. This batter was not like cookie dough but more like a thick cake batter. I made it in my cast iron skillet but next time may use a spring-form pan. It was delicious and got rave reviews! Consider sprinkling the top with confectioners next time.

Great recipe. I did make one change. I soaked the raisins in bourbon overnight. After draining the raisins I blended the remaining bourbon into a cup of softened butter to spread on the bread. WOW! Now a St. Patrick's Day favorite.

I couldn't find my recipe I got from a friend years ago, so I did a search and this one popped up. I'm so glad it did! I noticed it didn't use butter, as most of them do, which I liked because mixing in the butter is hard work for my arthritic hands. Then I read a review saying it was moist, not dry like some Irish breads can be. I guess it's the sour cream. Thats why I stopped looking and made this one. Anyway, I did it as written except I added 1/4 tsp. of orange oil and I used dried cranberries because I didn't have raisins. Everything else was the same. It came out so picture perfect in my small 2-3/4 qt Dutch oven. It took 1 hour to bake at 350 to an internal temperature of 205 degrees F. I baked it with the lid on about half the time. It rose so high, I couldn't keep the lid on. Perfect brown all around. It sliced beautifully while warm and had a smooth, velvety moist crumb, almost like a cake. Slathered with Irish Butter, it was incredible. Don't bother with any more searching, just make this one and save the recipe! I guarantee you will make it again soon.

Based on reviews, also cut the raisins back to 2 cups. This seemed a better proportion to me. Made in a cake pan. I personally could have eaten the entire loaf in one sitting. Loved this bread. Served with a hearty pork stew.
Best Irish soda bread ever and I have made many. Used 1 c. of cranberries, 1/2 cup raisins,& 1 1/2 c. golden raisins. Used my trusty cast iron skillet. Baked 65 min. Wonderful for breakfast.

This was a great launching point for the soda bread recipe of my dreams. The result was much more moist and tender than most soda breads I've tasted so that was a big plus. I think three cups of raisins was overdoing it, so I used two but it was still heavier on the raisins than I like. The full tablespoon of flour dusted on the top was also too excessive since it never really dissolved into the dough as much as pictured. I ended up with lots of raw flour on top.

Next time I think I will reduce the raisin content to a more typical one to one and a half cups, grease AND flour the pan for a crustier bottom, and either reduce or eliminate dusting the top with flour.

As the daughter of an Irish immigrant I’ve had plenty of DRY Irish Bread growing up. This is the very best I’ve had. I added a tsp. of nutmeg to the dry ingredients and 1 1/2 tsp. Vanilla to the wet ingredients. Maybe not authentic but who cares. It’s delicious. My friends call it Heavenly Bread.

Delicious! I made this tonight for the first time, along with corned beef and cabbage, and I am in love! I had never before even tasted Irish soda bread, and have been missing out. I have no idea if this recipe is consider authentic, but it is fantastic by any means. Before I put it in the oven, I brushed it with a mix of 1/4 melted butter and 1/4 cup buttermilk. I then glazed it 4 or 5 times while it was baking. It gave the bread a beautiful golden crust. I also omitted the raisins and caraway seeds, as I was looking for more of a basic bread. I will definitely be making this again!
I make this every year for St. Patrick's Day and everyone loves it! I have to make a double batch to keep everyone from fighting over the last piece.
Easy recipe. I prepare in 8" square pan. Slice and freeze. Delicious toasted with butter. I use 3.5 cups of raisins and a little extra caraway.
I followed the recipe with no changes. It was a crowd pleaser. Will make It again.
Most irish soda bread is so dry that I don't like it. This one was perfect! I leave out the caraway seeds because they're aren't my favorite. Delicious!

I'll take the credit, but I know the credit goes to this recipe. The best I've eaten (sorry mom, yours is best for life, but even you would agree with me on this one) I used 1 cup of currants (like mom used) 1 cup of golden and 1 cup dark raisins. Thanks!
I realized too late that I didn't have any caraway seeds, but this was still soooo good! Definitely a keeper.

I made this to go with our corned beef dinner and we ate it hot out of the oven. My dough was so soft and sticky I couldn't mark the 'X'on top and it rose up like a giant popover. Crunchy golden crust. Tender, yellow and slightly sweet inside. Only had 1 cup of raisins and it was enough. I wouldn't recommend omitting them.
